title: Clasp-retained partial denture
what: This is a removable denture on a thin metal frame. It is held to your own teeth by hooks or clasps.
why: When several teeth are missing and you still have your own teeth to hold it.
duration: making it usually takes several visits over a few weeks
tell_doctor: If you wore dentures before and how you got used to them

prepare.title: Treatment
prepare.text: Before the denture, teeth and gums are usually treated, and sometimes crowns are put on the supporting teeth.

prepare.title: Teeth
prepare.text: Brush your teeth before each visit.

bring: X-rays of your teeth, if you have them
Your old denture, if you have one
steps: The doctor examines your teeth and takes X-rays
Tries on the frame of the denture
Tooth color and shape are chosen
The denture is put on and adjusted
You are taught how to put it in and take it out
feel: In the first days the denture presses and speaking is hard
Lots of saliva in the first days, which passes
Getting used to it usually takes a few weeks
after: Take out and clean the denture after meals
At night, as your doctor says, usually take it out
Keep it in a clean case or in water
Do not bend the hooks yourself
Come for an adjustment if it rubs
red_flags: The denture rubbed a sore on your gum and it does not heal
The denture broke or no longer stays in place

faq.q: Can I sleep in the denture?
faq.a: Usually advised to take it out at night. Check with your doctor.
The hooks are sometimes visible on side teeth. Some clasps are less noticeable, so ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Denture visit tomorrow. Brush your teeth and bring your old denture, if you have one.
